s.note: Tuco marching Blondie across the desert
s.how: Cut 12 corn tortillas into wedges and fry at 180C until crisp, then toss in salt and chilli powder. Char 4 tomatoes and half an onion in a dry pan until blackened. Chop together with lime juice and salt for a smoky salsa and serve with the chips.

s.note: the gold buried in the grave
s.how: Slice 800g small potatoes into thick coins and toss in olive oil and salt. Spread on a tray and roast at 220C for 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Stir a crushed garlic clove into mayonnaise for aioli and serve the coins in a pile beside it.

m.note: the meal Angel Eyes eats at the farmer's table
m.how: Soak 400g dried borlotti beans overnight and drain. Soften a diced onion and garlic, then add the beans, a smoked ham hock, a can of crushed tomatoes, rosemary and water to cover. Simmer for 2 hours until thick, shred the ham back in and serve with Italian bread.

w.note: the graveyard where the gold is buried
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and cool slightly. Whisk 3 egg whites to soft peaks and whip 300ml cream. Fold the yolks into the chocolate, then fold in the cream and whites. Spoon into cups with a chocolate coin buried in each, chill and top with crushed chocolate biscuits.

d.how: Stir 60g demerara sugar with 60ml hot water until dissolved, then cool. For each drink, stir 60ml rye whisky, 10ml of the syrup and 2 dashes of orange bitters with ice for 30 seconds. Strain over a large ice cube in a heavy glass. Twist a strip of orange peel over the top and drop it in.
